draft_key_information_units.information: Profit before tax decreased to ISK 1,545 million in Q2 2026 from ISK 2,025 million in Q2 2025, a decline of ISK 480 million or 23.7%, driven by lower net fee income and one-off efficiency measure costs, despite resilient net interest income growth.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Profit before tax ISK 1,545 m. compared to ISK 2,025 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 480 m. from previous year, or 23.7%. Net interest income ISK 3,013 m. compared to ISK 2,962 m. in Q2 2025 Increasing by ISK 51 m. from previous year or 1.7%. Net fee and commission income ISK 1,416 m. compared to ISK 1,935 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 519 m. from previous year or 26.8%. Administrative expenses ISK 2,947 m. compared to ISK 2,981 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 34 m. from previous year or 1.1% despite ISK 112 m. one-off restructuring charge.

draft_key_information_units.information: Deposits surpassed ISK 200 billion for the first time, reaching ISK 201.2 billion at quarter-end, up 16.5% from year-end 2025, driven by retail deposits and public entities, while loans to customers grew to ISK 223.3 billion, up 7.6% from year-end 2025.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Deposits amounted to ISK 201.2 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 16.5% from year-end 2025. Loans to customers amounted to ISK 223.3 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by ISK 15.8 bn., or 7.6%, from year-end 2025.

draft_key_information_units.information: Net fee and commission income declined significantly to ISK 1,416 million in Q2 2026 from ISK 1,935 million in Q2 2025, a decrease of ISK 519 million or 26.8%, reflecting subdued capital markets activity and lower transaction volumes.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Net fee and commission income ISK 1,416 m. compared to ISK 1,935 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 519 m. from previous year or 26.8%. Activity in capital markets remained subdued during the quarter, with lower transaction volumes and softer client activity weighing on fee generation across all business lines.

draft_key_information_units.information: Capital adequacy ratio (CAR) stood at 23.0% at 30 June 2026, down from 26.8% at year-end 2025 primarily due to the ISK 10.2 billion special dividend payment in June, while maintaining a strong management buffer above regulatory requirements.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CAR of 23.0% at 30 June 2026, decreasing as special dividend was distributed in June. The bank continues to target a management buffer of 2% to 4% over current and anticipated CAR requirements.

draft_key_information_units.information: Liquidity position remains strong with LCR at 276% (well above 100% requirement) and NSFR at 137%, supported by high-quality liquid assets of ISK 76.4 billion (81% Level 1 assets).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) remains strong at 276%, well above the 100% regulatory requirement. NSFR stood at 137%. High-quality liquid assets (HQLA) amounted to ISK 76.4 bn., of which 81% were classified as Level 1 assets.

draft_key_information_units.information: Major strategic developments include CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson stepping down by year-end 2026, ongoing divestment of Straumur greiðslumiðlun hf., and announced efficiency measures expected to achieve annualized cost savings of ISK 300-400 million.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson to step down by year-end 2026. Sale of Straumur greiðslumiðlun hf. in progress. Efficiency measures announced in June expected to achieve annualised cost savings of ISK 300-400 m.

draft_key_information_units.information: Segment performance highlights strong loan growth in Commercial Banking (+ISK 6 bn QoQ) and Investment Banking (+nearly 4% QoQ), while UK operations show record loan book levels and advancing asset sales.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Commercial Banking: deposits increasing by ISK 12 bn. during Q2 (+8% QoQ), loans increasing in total by ISK 6 bn. during the quarter (+3%). Investment Banking: loan book grew by nearly 4% quarter-on-quarter. UK: loan book reaching an all-time high, Harpa completing additional PE deal, UK largest PE asset sale process expected to close before year-end.

draft_key_information_units.information: Six-month 2026 results show pre-tax profit from continuing operations increased by 23.0% YoY to ISK 3,354 million, driven by 6.8% YoY growth in net interest income and disciplined cost management.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Pre-tax profit from continuing operations increasing by 23.0% YoY to ISK 3,354 million in 6M 2026. Net interest income increased by 6.8% YoY. Administrative expenses amounted to ISK 5,961 m., a 1.8% decrease YoY.

evaluation.selection_rationale: Selected 8 units covering: 1) Headline profit performance decline with key drivers (D1), 2) Balance sheet growth in deposits/loans (D2), 3) Significant fee income decline (D3), 4) Capital adequacy position (D4), 5) Liquidity metrics (D5), 6) Major strategic developments including CEO succession and efficiency measures (D6), 7) Key segment performance highlights (D7), and 8) Six-month performance overview (D8). These represent the most material financial, operational, and strategic developments from Q2 2026, prioritizing YoY changes, balance sheet trends, capital position, and key strategic moves as required. Excluded routine boilerplate items like accounting policies, auditor information, and generic risk lists. Each unit is independently omittable and focuses on core content determining coverage.
